style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph of heavy corporate buyout legal documents on a matte dark oak desk surface. Top-down 90-degree view, even diffused daylight. A thick stack of muted, illegibly cropped contract papers rests slightly out of alignment to look handled. Resting on top of the printed documents as a paperweight is a small, unbranded matte-black smart home relay module with exposed terminal screws, next to a short clipped blue ethernet wire. Soft directional daylight casting subtle contact shadows, shallow depth of field, muted paper tones, modern premium editorial cover standard.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI elements, human hands, faces, logos
rationale: The narrative hinges entirely on what is written—and what is missing—in the €1.2 billion takeover paperwork. A document flatlay perfectly captures the contractual nature of the buyout, placing a physical smart relay onto the legal papers to represent the unwritten local interface.

subject: a small unbranded smart home relay module resting on a stack of corporate legal documents
core_thesis: The lasting value of a local-first home relies on the local interface you can test today, because the €1.2 billion takeover promise omits any guarantee for it.
core_conflict: Corporate buyout paperwork guaranteeing physical assets vs the unwritten guarantee of a local-first software interface.
